skill.name: wp-project-triage
skill.description: Inspect a WordPress repository and report its project type, tooling, tests, version hints, API usage, and recommended commands.
skill.summary: Classify WordPress repositories and identify tooling, tests, version hints, feature signals, and workflow recommendations.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals, Markdown code formatting, schema identifiers, and read-only filesystem inspection. The detector makes no network requests and does not execute generated command strings. Contextual risks remain in unbounded file reads, unsafe command recommendations, and absolute path disclosure.

remediation.issue: Recommended package and Composer commands may invoke repository-controlled scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as untrusted suggestions and require inspection of package scripts, Composer hooks, and executable targets before running them.

remediation.issue: File size limits are applied after complete files are loaded into memory.
remediation.suggestion: Check file size before reading or use bounded streaming reads to prevent memory exhaustion from unusually large files.

remediation.issue: The report includes the absolute repository root and other absolute local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Emit relative paths by default, or add an explicit option before including absolute paths in shareable reports.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Project Commands Recommended Without Validation
semantic_findings.description: The report recommends package, Composer, and PHPUnit commands from repository signals. Running them can execute repository-controlled scripts or lifecycle hooks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code clearly adds executable commands to recommendations without trust warnings. The detector does not execute them, which limits the immediate impact.

semantic_findings.title: File Limit Applied After Unbounded Read
semantic_findings.description: The reader loads each complete file before truncating its buffer. A crafted oversized source file can exhaust memory during repository inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation calls readFileSync before checking byteLength. This directly defeats the intended memory bound.

semantic_findings.title: Absolute Local Paths Included in Report
semantic_findings.description: The report includes the absolute current working directory and derived absolute paths. Shared output can disclose usernames or local directory structure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: process.cwd returns an absolute path, and the paths object places it in the emitted report. Disclosure requires the report to be shared.

content.value_statement: WordPress repositories often hide their project type, tooling, and test setup across many files. This skill scans local files and produces a consistent triage report.
actual_capabilities: Classifies plugins, themes, block projects, full sites, WordPress core, and Gutenberg repositories.
Detects Node package managers, WordPress scripts, Composer configuration, and installed vendor dependencies.
Identifies PHPUnit, wp-env, Playwright, and Jest test tooling from repository files.
Finds Interactivity API, Abilities API, InnerBlocks, WP-CLI, cache, and debugging signals.
Reports WordPress and Gutenberg version hints with their source files.
Suggests relevant lint, test, build, start, Composer, and PHPUnit commands without executing them.
limitations: Classification uses file and token heuristics, so unusual repository layouts can produce unknown or incomplete results.
Scans stop at configured depth and file limits, which can omit signals in large repositories.
The detector reads local files but does not validate behavior by running tests or project commands.
Recommended commands can invoke untrusted project scripts and require review before execution.

use_cases.title: Prepare a WordPress Change
use_cases.description: Identify project type, tooling, and available tests before editing an unfamiliar WordPress repository.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Intake
use_cases.description: Create a consistent technical inventory for plugins, themes, sites, core checkouts, and Gutenberg projects.

use_cases.title: Set Agent Guardrails
use_cases.description: Provide an AI coding agent with detected commands, version hints, and architecture signals before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Repository Inspection
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the current WordPress repository. Summarize its primary project type, detected tooling, tests, and recommended verification commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start work in an unfamiliar repository.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Classification Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Run WordPress project triage in {repo_path}. Explain each detected project kind and identify truncated scans or uncertain classifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review why a repository received its classification.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Verification Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage {repo_path} before implementation. Compare its Node, PHP, and test tooling, then propose a workflow using only detected commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan verification for a WordPress change.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Architecture and Command Trust
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {repo_path} for WordPress architecture signals. Validate the report against files, assess risky recommended scripts, and list unsupported assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform advanced intake for an untrusted repository.

output_examples.input: Triage a full WordPress site repository with performance tooling.

The scan found local performance and test tooling but did not execute validation.

output_examples.output: No plugin header, theme header, WordPress core structure, or wp-content directory was detected. Confirm the repository root and review scan limits.

best_practices: Run triage from the intended repository root and confirm the reported primary type.
Inspect package scripts, Composer hooks, and executable targets before running recommended commands.
Re-run triage after changes to manifests, block metadata, theme configuration, or test tooling.
anti_patterns: Do not treat heuristic matches as proof that a feature works correctly.
Do not execute recommended commands automatically in repositories that you do not trust.
Do not assume a truncated scan represents the complete repository.

faq.question: Does this skill modify repository files?
faq.answer: No. The detector performs read-only inspection and writes its report to standard output.

faq.question: Which WordPress project types can it identify?
faq.answer: It identifies plugins, must-use plugins, themes, block projects, full sites, WordPress core, Gutenberg, and unknown repositories.

faq.question: Does it run tests or build commands?
faq.answer: No. It reports detected commands and tooling but does not execute them.

faq.question: Why can a scan return unknown?
faq.answer: The selected root may lack recognized headers or structures, or relevant files may exceed scan limits.

faq.question: Can it detect WordPress versions?
faq.answer: It reports version hints from WordPress core and recognized Gutenberg package metadata when available.

faq.question: Is it safe to run on an untrusted repository?
faq.answer: The detector is read-only, but oversized files can affect memory. Review every recommended command before execution.
